q-81082.name: Question 1
q-81082.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $X?$

- $X∨(X∨Y)$
- $(Y∧X)∨X$
- $Y∨(X∧Y)$
q-81082.worked_solution:
The law that disjunction absorbs conjunction is stated as

$$
X∨(X∧Y)≡X.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is *not* logically equivalent to $X.$ This statement cannot be simplified using the absorption laws.

- Statement II is logically equivalent to $X.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(Y∧X)∨X & ≡X∨(Y∧X) \\  & ≡X∨(X∧Y) \\  & ≡X.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is *not* logically equivalent to $A.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Y∨(X∧Y) & ≡Y∨(Y∧X) \\  & ≡Y≢X.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

q-81276.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $C?$

- $B∨(B∨C)$
- $B∧(B∨C)$
- $C∧(B∨C)$
q-81276.worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
C∧(C∨B)≡C.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is *not* logically equivalent to $C.$ This statement cannot be simplified using the absorption laws.

- Statement II is *not* logically equivalent to $C.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}B∧(B∨C) & ≡B≢C.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $C.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}C∧(B∨C) & ≡C∧(C∨B) \\  & ≡C.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

q-81717.name: Question 3
q-81717.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $R?$

- $(T∨R)∧T$
- $R∧(T∨R)$
- $(R∨T)∧R$
q-81717.worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
R∧(R∨T)≡R.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is *not* logically equivalent to $R.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(T∨R)∧T & ≡T∧(T∨R) \\  & ≡T≢R.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is logically equivalent to $R.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}R∧(T∨R) & ≡R∧(R∨T) \\  & ≡R.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $R.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(R∨T)∧R & ≡R∧(R∨T) \\  & ≡R.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
